messages:
maria: Heads up — our payment worker started failing with AccessDenied on KMS decrypt after last night's key rotation. Putting logs here.

ashwin: Can you paste the error and which role it's using?

maria: Error from the app: 
```
An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/app-payment-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789 (Service: AWSKMS; Status Code: 400; Error Code: AccessDeniedException)
```

olivia: We rotated the CMK last night (auto-rotation + created a new key alias pointing to new key material) and reconfigured the pipeline to use the alias. But older object DEKs are still encrypted under the old key. Are those re-wrapped?

maria: The worker reads object metadata (DEK encrypted with CMK) and calls kms:Decrypt to unwrap the DEK, then decrypts object locally. So if the session principal can't call Decrypt on the old key ARN, it'll 403. The app uses an assumed role from the payment service account.

ashwin: Two common culprits: (1) key policy doesn't allow that assumed-role principal (cross-account / assumed principals need explicit allowance in key policy), or (2) there's a session policy / permission boundary limiting kms:Decrypt. Do you have the session policy snippet?

maria: Yes — the auth pipeline attaches a session policy that narrows permissions. Snippet: 
```
{\n  "Version": "2012-10-17",\n  "Statement": [\n    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObject"],"Resource":"*"},\n    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:ViaService":"ec2.us-west-2.amazonaws.com"}}}\n  ]\n}
```

olivia: Ah — kms:ViaService condition will only pass if the request is originating via the specified AWS service. Our worker runs in Fargate (sts-assumed role from custom OIDC token), so ViaService doesn't match. That would block. Also if the role is cross-account, check the key policy.

ashwin: Also worth checking grants: if the code creates a KMS grant dynamically for the session and immediately uses it, you must pass the GrantToken in the decrypt call if the grant was created in the same session. Otherwise use a key policy or long-lived grant.

maria: We're not creating grants on the fly — just relying on role/IAM + key policy. The account changed the alias to point to the rotated CMK (new key id). The session policy references the old key id explicitly. I think the mismatch is the old key id vs alias vs new key id plus ViaService condition.

ashwin: Quick tests to run: 
- Verify caller identity: `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile prod`
- Try decrypt directly as that role (impersonate or assume-role with session) and run: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://wrapped.key --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789` and see the error.
- If you created a grant in the same flow: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob ... --grant-tokens "<grant-token>"`

kms-bot: Key rotation completed for alias/keys/payment-cmk -> new key arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/ef01-2345-6789-abcd at 2026-03-19T03:12:00Z

olivia: If the rotation replaced the key resource entirely (we sometimes create a new CMK and repoint alias), old ARNs still govern DEKs. You'll need either: re-encrypt DEKs with the new key (rewrap), or ensure the role has kms:Decrypt permission on the old key ARN until all data is rewrapped.

ashwin: For cross-account: key policy must include the principal ARN of the assumed role (not the role name in other account) and allow kms:Decrypt. Example key policy statement: 
```
{\n  "Sid":"AllowPaymentRole",\n  "Effect":"Allow",\n  "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/app-payment-role"},\n  "Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],\n  "Resource":"*"\n}
```

maria: Ran the impersonation test. Confirmed ViaService condition blocks the call, and the old key ARN wasn't in the session policy. So fix options: remove/special-case ViaService condition, or add the assumed-role principal to key policy for the old key.

sre-rotation: Note: if you add a key policy allow, avoid broad "Principal":"*" opens. Prefer specific role ARNs and least privilege. Also document rewrap plan and schedule to decrypt+re-encrypt DEKs, or switch object meta to alias and trigger lazy rewrap on read.

maria: We're going to add the role ARN to the old key's policy temporarily and run a background job to rewrap all DEKs to the new key alias. After that we'll remove the explicit old-key grant.

ashwin: Also add an audit entry and CloudTrail filter for KMS Decrypt failures during the migration window so we can monitor any stragglers.

maria: ✅ Update: added principal to key policy, migration job started, objects are being rewrapped. Will keep the key policy change for 24 hours while we confirm. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
